correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed full n,m,k proof. Put r=m−k. In each base m² block a nonempty row clique must have c_i≥r; two empty rows force undominated off-diagonal vertex (i,j) because its sole external neighbor (j,i) is likewise unselected. If one row empty, domination forces a selected cross-link in all other rows and hence c_j≥r+1; block occupancy ≥(m−1)(r+1)≥mr. Every block contributes ≥mr, giving ≥r m^(n−1). For the upper bound, a symmetric r-regular residue relation with either uniform present or absent diagonal selects exactly r elements per row; every extra link connects vertices with both membership equal, so selected vertices have exactly k excluded neighbors inside own clique. n=1 is K_m. Independently brute-forced n=2,m=2,3 with feasible optima 2,6,3 for (m,k)=(2,1),(3,1),(3,2), corroborating but not replacing universal proof.
